step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Data ingestion (top block): raw CSV/Excel files are uploaded to the first S3 bucket; a Lambda is triggered to validate them and writes the validated copy to a different S3 folder; a second Lambda is then triggered to process the validated data and ingest it into OpenSearch. The whiteboard arrow between the second Lambda and the validated S3 is drawn Lambda-to-S3, but the audio says the validated copy triggers that Lambda, so it is recorded as an S3-to-Lambda trigger. 2) The two OpenSearch icons (ingestion and retrieval blocks) are the same Graviton2 cluster, so they are fused into one node. 3) Data retrieval (bottom block): the hand-drawn FE (Angular) and BE (Python) boxes are active participants described in the audio, so they are recorded as ThirdParty nodes. Web path: user to front end, back to the browser, then to the back end, then to the data layer, with the response returning via the back end. Mobile path: user directly to the back end, then the data layer, then the response. 4) The data layer is OpenSearch plus RDS; the whiteboard shows bidirectional arrows between BE and RDS, and the audio only says 'data layer', so the BE-to-OpenSearch edge is inferred from that wording. 5) Large reports (more than 10,000 records): the report is uploaded to the second-block S3 bucket, the user is notified via SES, and downloads it with a pre-signed URL. The audio does not name who uploads the report or calls SES; the back end is assumed. 6) The generic user is kept as the system entry point (web and mobile). No node is created for the source of the CSV/Excel files because it is not identified.

graph.name: Cybex: Event-Driven Trade Data Processing with Amazon OpenSearch
graph.notes: Novantec built this for Cybex (export/import trade data and reports). Event-driven ingestion from S3 through Lambda into OpenSearch on Graviton2. Records grew from 1.5 billion to about 5 billion (more than 3.5x) on the same architecture, with reports of 15-20 complex parameters served in 2-4 seconds. Graviton2 saves 25-30% of operating cost, roughly $100K. Users retrieve data via a web app (Angular front end) or a mobile app, both through a Python back end. Reports over 10,000 records are delivered asynchronously via S3, SES and a pre-signed URL.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: End user who accesses trade data and reports through the web application (browser) or the mobile application.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Raw Data)
nodes.notes: Bucket where raw data in CSV or Excel format is uploaded. Initial volume about 1.5 billion records, now about 5 billion.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Validation)
nodes.notes: Triggered on raw data upload to validate the data. Discrepancies are highlighted; otherwise a validated copy is written to a different S3 folder.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Validated Data)
nodes.notes: Different folder within the S3 buckets that holds the validated copy of the data.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Processing)
nodes.notes: Triggered once the validated copy is available. Processes the validated data and ingests it into the OpenSearch cluster.

nodes.name: Amazon OpenSearch (Graviton2)
nodes.notes: OpenSearch cluster on Graviton2 instances, saving 25-30% of operating cost (about $100K). Query templates are mapped to relevant indexes, OpenSearch analyzers fine-tune queries, and an aggregation layer serves complex reports such as trend analysis. Serves reports with 15-20 complex parameters in 2-4 seconds over about 5 billion records.

nodes.name: Front-End Application (Angular)
nodes.notes: Web front-end application developed in Angular, accessed through the web browser.

nodes.name: Back-End Application (Python)
nodes.notes: Back-end application developed in Python. Receives requests from the browser and the mobile app, queries the data layer, and returns the response to the user.

nodes.name: Amazon RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database in the data retrieval block, part of the data layer accessed by the back end.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Reports)
nodes.notes: Bucket where large reports (more than 10,000 records) are uploaded for download via a pre-signed URL.

nodes.name: Amazon SES
nodes.notes: Sends an email notification to the user to download the large report using the pre-signed URL.
